interactions.title: The recalled bargain and moving prison
lines: DM: Last spring, the embittered adventurer Hulda received a 400-year-old deed of inheritance. Perfect. Written in oddly contemporary language to a manor house at the wild northern edges of the Duchy of Tellim.
DM: There was one condition: go through the door in the cellar of the house, and convince the Fae lord on the other side to break a promise once made.
DM: Lord Endless Ending had been tricked into his compact by the wizard Thalestria, head of the Drankorian order Arithrimos Lamperum in the waning days of the Empire.

DM: Each time a clock she gave him struck zero, Lord Ending would send a mortal guest at his party through the doors of her house. That compact has held to the present, 700 years later, though for the Feylord, it was merely struck earlier, in the same endless celebration he still hosts.

DM: Hulda hires the party, who travel to the Feylord's Revel, where Tarek steals a yet-to-be-disclosed possession of that lord, and the party meets guests from across centuries, including a curious rakshasa, tigerman.

DM: The Fae is unable to break his promise but asks them to bring him the key to the prison door at the center of the house. Presumably because if he breaks it and the prisoner goes free, his promise becomes irrelevant.
DM: Joined by Menestheus, a member of Thalestria's party who she left behind when she made the bargain, the group enters the house of 27 rooms.

DM: Surrounding a central prison chamber, the Order built the house as a magical and mechanical device to untether the central prison room from the world around it and to keep the physical and the temporal location of that central room constantly changing. If it stopped moving somehow, the prisoner would quickly escape.

DM: Each movement through a doorway between rooms in the house shifts the physical or temporal coordinates of the prison. And in that way, the randomness of mortal choices kept the prisoner from knowing where or when they were or what to expect was coming. And the steady supply of mortals, by Lord Endless Ending, has kept it in constant motion to this day.
